grid.description: Rules across the plot at every mark.

ticks.description:
Roughly how many marks to aim for. The real count is whatever lands on
round numbers near it.

anyOf.description: Shorthand for a paragraph holding this text.

BlockObject.description: The object form of [`Block`]. The string form is a paragraph of that text.

sides.description: Which edges to draw. All four by default.

Box.description: The frame's own box blocks the text.

blocks.description:
A cell holds blocks, not a string: two paragraphs and a rule inside one
cell is ordinary in teaching material, and this way the whole of
`flow_blocks` is reused rather than a second text path invented.

x.description: Explicit column. Absent means the next free slot, filling row by row.

CellAlign.description:
Where a cell's content sits in the space its row gives it.

A vocabulary of its own rather than the frame's `VerticalAlign`: a frame
can justify its paragraphs and has nothing to align a baseline *with*,
while a cell is the other way round. Sharing one enum would mean two
values that are meaningless wherever they are read.

oneOf.description:
The cell's first line sits on the same baseline as the other cells in
its row that ask for the same. The CSS rule, and the one that makes a
table of headings and numbers read straight when the type sizes differ.

Channel.description: A field, and what it drives.

field.description: Name of the field in the data.

kind.description:
What the field means. Absent means "read it off the data", which is
only ever asked when the answer is not in doubt: a field holding no
numbers at all cannot go on a continuous scale, so it is categorical.

Optional rather than defaulting to quantitative, because the default
was wrong in the commonest case there is. `{"field": "mes"}` over
months is what anyone writes first, and reading it as a quantity gave
a numeric axis over text and a bar chart with nothing to stand on.

title.description: Shown beside the axis. Absent means the field's own name.

clip.description: Clip content to the frame box.

corner.description:
How a corner with a radius turns: an arc, or a straight cut.

One flag for the four corners, not four: which corners turn is already
said by the radius, so a per-corner style would be a second way of
saying the same thing. A box that cuts only its bottom-right corner —
the shape didactic concept boxes use — is a radius on that corner alone
plus `corner: "cut"`.

The cut reaches the fill and the border, which are outlines. It does
**not** reach `clip`: a clip is a rect plus radii in the display list,
and giving it an arbitrary outline is a wider change than a chamfer
justifies. A frame that both clips and cuts clips to the rounded shape.

data.description: Inline observations. Ignored when `dataset` is set.

dataset.description:
Sugar: pull the rows from `resources.data` instead of `data`.

The same pair `blocks` and `story` already are on a text frame, and for
the same reason: two charts of the same numbers should not be two
copies of the numbers. Called `dataset` and not `series`, because a
series is one line inside a chart and confusing the two would cost an
explanation every time.

palette.description: Colours for the series, in order. Absent means the built-in palette.

Component.description:
A reusable group of frames with named slots.

The frames are positioned from the component's own top-left corner, at
the `size` the component was designed at. An instance may be drawn at
another size; each frame's [`Follow`](super::frame::Follow) says how it
moves or stretches with the difference.

description.description: What this block is for, in the author's words — the writer model reads it.

label.description: Human-facing label shown in the editor's component list.

size.description: `[width, height]` the frames were designed at.

Contour.description:
A silhouette blocks the text.

`points` is a closed ring in `0..1` coordinates relative to the
frame's rect, so it survives resizing the frame. It is stored as a
ring rather than a pixel mask because a document is authored, edited
and diffed by people.

CornerStyle.description: What a corner does with its radius.

oneOf.description: A quarter-circle arc. What every box did before this existed.
A straight line across the corner, consuming the radius on both edges.

Corners.description: Corner radii clockwise from the top-left: one value, [tl, tr], [tl, tr, br, bl], or a map. Nothing means square corners.

Encoding.description: Which field drives which visual channel.

color.description: Splits the data into series, one colour each.

FieldKind.description: What a field means, which is what decides its scale.

oneOf.description: A number, on a continuous scale.
A name, one band or one position each.

Follow.description:
How a component's frame tracks the instance's size.

The difference between the instance rect and the component's `size` is
`dw × dh`. A frame with `x` shifts right by `dw`; with `w` it grows by
`dw`; likewise `y` and `h`. A title band therefore says `{ "w": true }`,
the body says `{ "w": true, "h": true }`, and a badge pinned to the
bottom-right says `{ "x": true, "y": true }`.

oneOf.description: Treated as italic when the family has no separate oblique face.

Frame.description:
A positioned box on a page.

`rect` is in points, measured from the top-left corner of the **page**
(not the margin box), with `y` growing downward. Inside a group, it is
measured from the group's own top-left corner.

GridLine.description: A rule drawn along a grid line, independent of the cells.

at.description: Which boundary: 0 is before the first track, `n` is after the last.

axis.description: `horizontal` runs along a row boundary, `vertical` along a column one.

from.description: Track index the rule starts at; absent means the first.

to.description: Track index the rule stops before; absent means past the last.

GroupFrame.description: A frame whose children are positioned relative to its own origin.

clip.description: Clip content to the frame box.

baseline.description: Offset of the image bottom from the text baseline.

InlineObject.description: The object form of [`Inline`]. The string form is a text run.

offset.description: Distance below the baseline. Defaults to the font's underline position.

width.description: Absent means "fill the rest of the line".

InstanceFrame.description: A placed copy of a component.

slots.description: Content for the component's slots, by slot name.

Len.description: A length: a number of points, or a string with a unit ("18mm", "1cm", "12pt", "16px", "0.5in").

anyOf.description: A multiple of the font size.

Marker.description: A label placed before a paragraph — bullet, number, letter, anything.

gap.description: Gap between the marker and the text. Ignored when `width` is set.

hanging.description: When true, wrapped lines align with the text, not with the marker.

width.description: Fixed width of the marker column.

Master.description:
A page template: frames stamped onto every page that references it, plus
optional geometry.

frames.description: Painted beneath the page's own frames.

language.description: BCP-47 tag, e.g. `"pt-BR"`. Emitted into the PDF catalog.

Overflow.description: What to do with content that does not fit in its frame.

oneOf.description: Drop it, and report the frame as overset (InDesign's red `+`).
Grow the frame downward to fit.

style.description: Style scope for every frame on this page.

bleed.description: Extra area beyond the trim, for print bleed.

facing.description: Treat pages as left/right spreads, mirroring inner/outer margins.

anyOf.description: A named size ("A4", "A5", "letter", "livro-didatico", …), optionally suffixed " landscape".

PanelBlock.description:
Blocos dentro de uma moldura, que flui com o texto.

A moldura de um frame não serve aqui: um frame é posicionado em coordenada
absoluta, e por isso não desce junto com o parágrafo que o antecede nem
quebra quando a página acaba. Um destaque, um quadro de atividade ou uma
citação recuada precisam das duas coisas ao mesmo tempo — pintura própria e
fluxo — e é essa a lacuna que este bloco fecha.

Antes dele, a única forma de ter moldura no fluxo era uma tabela de uma
célula. Funcionava, mas custava caro: tabela não tem raio de canto, e a
borda tinha de ser escrita como quatro linhas de grade, que duas caixas
vizinhas então compartilhavam.

corner.description: O que o canto faz com o raio: arco, ou corte reto. Ver `Frame::corner`.

inset.description: Espaço entre a moldura e o conteúdo.

minHeight.description:
Altura mínima da moldura, borda inclusa.

A moldura cresce com o conteúdo; isto lhe dá um piso. É o que permite a
um editor deixar um quadro de atividade com espaço de sobra para o
aluno escrever, sem encher o painel de blocos vazios para empurrá-lo.

Não é altura fixa: conteúdo que passe do piso continua crescendo, e um
piso maior do que o que resta na coluna é limitado ao que resta — uma
moldura que passasse da mancha empurraria para fora o que vem depois,
sem que nada na página dissesse por quê.

origin.description:
Onde o autor escreveu este painel na lista de blocos.

Um painel que continua na página seguinte é refluído numa lista nova,
cujos índices recomeçam; sem isto o editor perderia de vista de qual
painel a continuação veio. Mesma razão que `TableBlock::origin`.

radius.description: Os quatro cantos, no sentido horário a partir do superior esquerdo.

style.description:
`spaceBefore` e `spaceAfter` valem para a moldura inteira, e
`keepWithNext` prende o painel ao bloco seguinte.

Paragraph.description: A run of inline content laid out as a sequence of lines.

id.description:
Stable identity, echoed into the display list so the editor can map a
painted glyph back to its source.

marker.description: Bullet, number or label placed before the first line.

Rect.description: [x, y, w, h] in points from the page's top-left corner, or { x, y, w, h }.

RepeatRows.description: Rows that repeat when the table breaks across pages.

continued.description:
Shown in place of `rows` on the pages where the table is *continuing*
— not on the page it begins, for a header, nor the page it ends on,
for a footer.

Named for the continuation rather than for the exception, which is what
makes one field serve both ends. `rows` are real rows of the table and
appear where they were written: a header at the top of the first page,
a total at the foot of the last. This is the other thing — the smaller
heading a reader meets halfway down a table, the "(continua)" under a
page that has not finished. Called `first` it would have meant the
opposite thing at each end of the table.

repeat.description: Off when the rows should appear once and not again.

rows.description: How many rows from the top — or, for a footer, from the bottom.

Resources.description:
Reusable definitions referenced by name from the raw core.

Everything here is optional: a document that inlines all its styles and
content never needs a `resources` object at all.

colors.description:
Named colours, so a palette change is a one-line edit.

Any colour field may say `"@name"` to take the entry of that name; the
reference is resolved before the document is parsed, so the engine
only ever sees a literal colour.

components.description:
Named groups of frames with slots — the didactic boxes of a collection.

A frame `{"type": "instance", "component": name, "slots": {…}}` is
replaced by the component's frames before layout, with each slot's
content placed in the frame that declares that slot.

data.description:
Named tables of observations, so two charts of the same numbers are not
two copies of the numbers.

stories.description: Named text flows that can be threaded across frames.

styles.description:
Named paragraph/character styles, referenced with `"use": "h1"` or
`{"extends": "h1"}`. Sorted for reproducible output.

width.description: Fraction of the column width, 0–1. Defaults to the full column.

ScaleKind.description: Which scale to build, when the field's kind is not the answer wanted.

ScaleSpec.description:
The author overriding what the field's kind would have chosen.

Every field optional, and an absent one means "decide for me". A chart that
has to state its scale to draw at all would be a chart nobody writes twice.

categories.description:
The categories, in the order they should appear. Absent means the order
they are met in the data, which is the order the author typed them.

domain.description: Lower and upper bound, for a continuous scale.

nice.description: Widen the domain to round numbers. On by default for a continuous axis.

paddingInner.description: Gap between neighbouring bands, as a share of the step.

paddingOuter.description: Gap before the first band and after the last.

zero.description:
Whether the scale must reach zero.

Absent means the mark decides, and a bar decides yes: a bar chart that
does not start at zero lies about the proportions, and teaching
material is the worst place for that.

ShapeFrame.description: A frame that draws a vector primitive using the frame's own fill and border.

clip.description: Clip content to the frame box.

corner.description:
How a corner with a radius turns: an arc, or a straight cut.

One flag for the four corners, not four: which corners turn is already
said by the radius, so a per-corner style would be a second way of
saying the same thing. A box that cuts only its bottom-right corner —
the shape didactic concept boxes use — is a radius on that corner alone
plus `corner: "cut"`.

The cut reaches the fill and the border, which are outlines. It does
**not** reach `clip`: a clip is a rect plus radii in the display list,
and giving it an arbitrary outline is a wider change than a chamfer
justifies. A frame that both clips and cuts clips to the rounded shape.

rotation.description: Clockwise rotation in degrees, about the frame's centre.

slot.description:

of that name replaces a text frame's `blocks` or an image frame's
`src`. Meaningless outside `resources.components`.

oneOf.description: A straight line from the top-left to the bottom-right of the frame box.

SlotValue.description:
What fills a slot.

A bare string is a paragraph of that text; a list is the blocks of a text
frame; `{"src": …}` is the image of an image frame.

offset.description: Which row of each group is filled.

background.description: Painted behind the text run itself (highlighting), not behind the frame.

baselineShift.description: Raises (positive) or lowers (negative) the run relative to the baseline.

extends.description: Name of a style declared in `resources.styles` to inherit from.

fontScale.description: Scales the font size for this run — used for sub/superscripts.

keepWithNext.description: Keep this paragraph on the same fragment as the next one.

lineHeight.description: A number is a multiple of the font size; a string is an absolute length.

align.description:
`right` ends the text that follows at the stop instead of starting it
there. With no `to`, the stop is the column's right edge, so a table of
contents keeps its page numbers flush however wide the frame becomes.

leader.description:
Drawn across the gap the tab opens: `.` dots, `-` dashes, `_` a solid
line. Anything else is read as dots.

to.description:
Absolute x position within the column to advance to. When absent, the
next multiple of `defaultStop` is used — or, for a right tab, the
column's right edge.

TabAlign.description: Which side of the text after a tab lines up with the stop.

TableBlock.description:
A grid of cells.

A block rather than a frame, because a table has to flow with the text
around it: it follows the paragraph before it, and when the page runs out
it continues on the next one.

columns.description:
One entry per column. An empty list means the columns are inferred
from the widest row, all of them automatic.

footer.description: Rows repeated at the foot of every page the table continues past.

header.description: Rows repeated when the table continues on another page.

inset.description: Padding inside every cell, unless the cell says otherwise.

lines.description:
Rules drawn between tracks, independent of any cell.

A rule under the heading is one declaration here, not a border
repeated in eight cells — the `booktabs` model, and the reason its
tables read.

rows.description: One entry per row; missing entries are automatic.

stripe.description: Alternating row fills, so striping is not written into every row.

TextFrame.description: A frame that lays out blocks of text.

autoFlow.description:
Keep generating pages until the content runs out.

When this frame overflows and no `threadNext` is set, the engine appends
a page modelled on the one this frame sits on — same size, margins and
master — carrying a copy of this frame, and continues the flow there.
This is what turns a story plus one page into a book.

Ignored when `threadNext` is set: an explicit chain wins.

blocks.description: Inline content. Ignored when `story` is set.

clip.description: Clip content to the frame box.

columnRule.description:
A vertical line in the middle of each gap, as tall as the taller of the
two columns it separates. Absent: the gap alone separates them.

corner.description:
How a corner with a radius turns: an arc, or a straight cut.

One flag for the four corners, not four: which corners turn is already
said by the radius, so a per-corner style would be a second way of
saying the same thing. A box that cuts only its bottom-right corner —
the shape didactic concept boxes use — is a radius on that corner alone
plus `corner: "cut"`.

The cut reaches the fill and the border, which are outlines. It does

and giving it an arbitrary outline is a wider change than a chamfer
justifies. A frame that both clips and cuts clips to the rounded shape.

size other than the one the component was designed at.

id.description: Stable identity. Auto-assigned during validation when absent.

ignoreWrap.description:
Lay this text out as if no frame on the page carried a wrap.

The escape hatch every wrap needs: a caption sitting on top of its own
photograph would otherwise be shoved off it by the very picture it
describes. InDesign spells this "ignore text wrap", and it is a
property of the text, not of the picture — one frame opts out without
changing what the picture does to everything else.

name.description: Human-facing label shown in the editor's layer list.

padding.description: Inner spacing between the frame box and its content.

radius.description:
Corner radii in points, clockwise from the top-left.

A bare number still rounds all four the same, which is what most boxes
want and what every document written before corners were separable
says.

rotation.description: Clockwise rotation in degrees, about the frame's centre.

slot.description:
Inside a component: the slot this frame receives. An instance's slot
of that name replaces a text frame's `blocks` or an image frame's
`src`. Meaningless outside `resources.components`.

story.description: Sugar: pull content from `resources.stories` instead of `blocks`.

threadNext.description: Sugar: id of the frame that receives content overflowing this one.

TrackSize.description: "auto", a fixed length, "1fr" (a share of the leftover) or "25%" (a share of the whole).

Value.description:
One cell of data.

Untagged, so a row is written the way anyone would write it: `120` is a
number, `"jan"` is text, `null` is a hole. Holes are kept rather than
rejected — real data has them, and a chart that refuses to load because one
month is missing is less useful than one that draws the other eleven.

VerticalAlign.description: Vertical placement of content inside a frame.

oneOf.description: Stretch inter-paragraph spacing so the content fills the frame.

Wrap.description:
Text wrap: the space a frame denies to the text around it.

The shape lives in the document rather than being read back from the
image's pixels at layout time. Tracing a silhouette is authoring work — it
belongs to the editor, where a person can see and correct it. An engine
that decoded pixels would stop being deterministic across platforms, and
the PDF would stop matching the canvas.

padding.description: Clearance in points, held between the text and the shape.

description:
A whole document: the single input to both the PDF emitter and the browser
painter.

page.description: Geometry applied to pages that do not override it.
